publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The calculation of transmission system reliability for planning has been implemented in a computer program, the Transmission Reliability Analysis Program (TRAP). Based on the concept of Load Supplying Capability (USC) of a transmission network, TRAP provides quantitative information concerning network adequacy. These reliability indices, which measure the capacity of a transmission system and the probability that transmission events result in loss of load, are illustrated using the EPRI Synthetic System D.

articleTitle: Use of Computer Graphics in Data Management Systems for Distribution Network Planning in "Electricite de France" (E.D.F.)
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Two data management systems for distribution network planning (L.V. and M.V. systems) are used by many EDF Distribution Centers.

articleTitle: Shunt Capacitor Bank Protection Methods
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A "Guide for Protection of Shunt Capacitor Banks," ANSI/IEEE Standard C37.99-1980, has been prepared recently by the, Power System Relaying Committee to assist in the effective application of relays for the protection of shunt capacitor banks used in substations. The various protective considerations along with recommended and alternate methods of protection for the most commonly used capacitor bank configurations are covered. The purpose of this paper is to review some of the highlights of the guide to familiarize the industry with the scope and usefulness of this new document, and to invite considered discussion for the purpose of improving this guide in the future.

articleTitle: Development and Field Experience of Digital Protection and Control Equipment in Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In applying microelectronic techniques to protective and control equipment in the power system, there is an important subject to be solved, which is the assurerance of long-term reliability. From this viewpoint, countermeasures against environmental conditions, for example temperature rise, electro-magnetic interference and dust are reconsidered.

articleTitle: Direct Fault Location in Electrical Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Fault location in electric power transmission or distribution systems is essential to the maintenance of reliable and continuous service. As a result, increased effort is being focused on fault locating procedures in distribution systems such that faults may be automatically isolated and unfaulted feeders restored to service in a short time. Presented is an^ alternative to existing fault locating procedures based upon the concept of the adjoint circuit and the recently derived theorem on the maximum number of independent simulations in N-port circuits. The theoretical approach is described for open circuit, short circuit, and mixed open and short circuit faults, followed by a numerical example applied to fault location in radial distribution feeders.

articleTitle: Data Base Model for Distribution Facilities
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In this paper we describe an electric facilities data base model which: - Provides data for engineering analysis, accounting and map production. - provides efficient access to data by electric network or by area. - has been implemented at several utilities. The model presented in this paper in incorporated in two IBM programs: Interactive Geo-Facilities Graphic Support (IGGS) and Geo-Facility Data Base Support (GDBS). The programs - provide for the storage of geographic and alphanumeric information, including electric facilities and land features. - support selective updating and display of both the geographic and alphanumeric data using an interactive workstation.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Cable Ampacity with Four or More Conductors in Rigit Galvanized Steel Conduit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The allowable ampacity of four or more low voltage conductors in isolated rigid galvanized conduit in air can be practically determined from ICEA S-135 if the cables are identical. The National Electrical Code (NEC) has been used to determine the derated ampacity of four or more low voltage conductors in conduit, but the theoretical or empirical basis for the derating factors is not contained or referenced in the NEC.

articleTitle: An Integrated Software System for Power System Operation-Control and-Planning
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper presents the structure of the software and the data of an integrated system for use in power generation and distribution control centres. The integrated system renders a uniform communication between operators and system engineers on one hand and supervisory control, security monitoring and short/medium term planning software on the other hand. The paper concentrates on the power application software (PAS) and describes the functions available in different console modes. A classification of PAS modules is introduced and the external and internal data interfaces are discussed.

articleTitle: Thyristor Devices for Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Thyristors of higher voltage and current ratings containing new gate and self-protective features are being developed at General Electric with EPRI (Electric Power Research Institute) support. Some of the more important of these are described in this paper. Devices include light triggered thyristors (LTT's), now at the 5 and 6KV level, and asymr metric light triggered thyristors (ALTT's) with 50% higher surge capability and 50% faster turn-off times than a regular thyristor. New features include "controlled turn-on", which protects thyristors from destructive di/dt during turn-on, and " voltage breakover" (VBO) protection, which prevents destructive avalanche current turn-on.

articleTitle: Various Practical Results Concerning the Operation of Inverter Fed Self Controlled Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper gives some informto about the effect of the value of the smoo- thing reactance on torque ripple and amorthing r winding current variations. Valuetisseur ap angles are compared in the two ca- ses of a battery supply and of a rectifier ly. The ripple in the torque, line voltage and phase current, are studied in the case of a rectifier supply. The safety of operation is considered from the points of view of characteristic angles and of a " potential peak short circuit current" which i defined in the paper, and which expresses the ability of the machine to ensure a natu- commutation.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of an Automatic Stability Prediction and Control (ASPAC) for a Synchronous Generator by Air Gap Flux
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the basic principles and test results of a newly developed equipment. It is concerned with automatic prediction and control of stability, for a synchronous generator by using its air gap flux directly.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Low Current Interrupting Capability in Self-Interruption GCB
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An arc chamber with negative pressure device was developed for the breaker without puffer action to improve the interrupting capability at low current region. The function of the device was analyzed by making use of a digital simulation program developed for this purpose. The results of the simulation was verified by the interruption test of a breaker with negative pressure device. The interruption test was performed at 84 kV under IEC standards and showed that the arc chamber can cover the full range of the interrupting current.

articleTitle: A Solid State Gas Density Monitor for Gas Insulated Substation Equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A solid state gas density monitor has been developed for SF6 service in gas-insulated substation equipment that is based on principles and construction techniques similar to ionization-type fire alarms. The monitor has a resolution of .7kPa (.1 psi) at 20°C. and, depending on ion chamber voltage and geometry, exhibits a linearity of ±1. to ±4. kPa (±.15 to ±.6 psi) at 20°C. over the density range 0.20 to 0.66 MPa (30 to 95 psia) at 20°C. The monitor incorporates two level contact closure actuated by gas density falling below one of two pre-set alarm limits, and an LCD read-out for visual monitoring and instrument calibration. The display presents density in terms of equivalent psia at 68°F (20°C.).

articleTitle: Failure of Electromagnetic Voltage Transformer Due to Sustained Over-Voltage on Switch off - Preventive Measures
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The damage to a 220 KV electromagnetic voltage transformer (EMVT) due to sustained over-voltage on switch-off by a circuit breaker (CB) fitted with grading capacitors, and subsequent studies for the steady-state period have already been reported [1]. In this paper, the pre-steady state period is analyzed and excellent agreement shown between field and analytical results. The concerned parameters for various makes of CB's, EMVT's and bus-bar capacitance have been collected and a. number of studies conducted. It is concluded that the control of. the EMVT saturation characteristic is superior compared to the measures su, ggested earlier to prevent such over-voltages. A suitable saturation characteristic for the worst case has been identified.

articleTitle: Electrical Features of the Bath County Pumped - Storage Project
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Bath County Pumped Storage Project is scheduled for full commercial operation on the VEPCO system in October, 1986. This paper describes the significant features of the major electrical equipment. Particular emphasis is placed on the considerations which led to the selection of static, variable-frequency starting of the units as pumps and to the use of a gas-insulated (GIS) 500-kV switchyard.

articleTitle: Dyanamic Behavior of Gas-Blasted Arcs in SF6-N2 Mixture
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The arc quenching phenomenon in an SF6-N2 mixture was analyzed by using the simulation program developed by the authors. The gas flow from the cylinder to the arc was investigated as a function of SF6-N2 mixing ratio in relation to the configuration of the arc chamber. The pressure rise in the cylinder was measured to confirm the result of the simulation by varying the SF6-N2 mixing ratio. The result of the simulation suggests that the desirable configuration of arc chamber should be changed depending upon the mixing ratio of SF6-N2 mixture.

articleTitle: Abnormal Vibration Problems in Large Turbine-Driven Generators and Their Solutions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Some unusual causes of abnormal vibration in large turbine-driven generators, are presented along with extensive test data on a 416 MVA generator equipped with many internal thermocouples and vibration transducers. The behavior of this and other large generators after a period of operation appeared to indicate buckling of the stator laminations is occurring which lowers the natural frequency of the core structure in the elliptical vibration mode. Moreover, experience has also shown that internal temperatures within the core structure sometimes affect the natural core frequency.

articleTitle: Determination of Stress Cone Profiles for Termination of High Voltage, XLPEI Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A numerically based method is used for deriving an expression for the stress cone profile of termiated high voltage cables. The application to a compact 138 kV XLPEI cable with XLPE molded termination is demonstrated The profile expression is in terms of the cable insulation radius and the specified maximum longitudinal electric stress at the profile.

articleTitle: Distribution Transformer Primary Fuse Coordination
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Successful application of primary fuses on distribution transformers depends on several factors, one of which is coordination. Proper coordination implies proper sequence of operation of protective devices. Proper sequence of operation depends on consideration of system characteristics, transformer characteristics, and fuse characteristics. This paper reviews each of these characteristics.

articleTitle: Degradation Process of Grease Due to SF6 Gas Dissociation Products
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: It is known that some insulating materials are degraded due to dissociation products of SF6 gas. Many studies related to the degradation of insulating materials have been accomplished. But no studies related to sealing materials, for instance (lubricating) grease and rubber have been made.

articleTitle: Test Results of AC Superconducting Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: All the major components of an ac superconducting power transmission system have been developed. A summary of test results during the developmental stages is given. A Test Facility designed to demonstrate and evaluate cables rated for 138 kV, 1000 MVA 3 øservice is under construction. Most of the equipment has been installed and tested; results are presented.

articleTitle: Field Experience with Harmonics Injecting Equipment in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The authors discuss field experience with three ac-dc converter installations. A rectifier and two self-commutated inverters comprise the evaluated equipment. Each case deals with slightly different aspects in the application of converters on power systems. The three cases compliment each other to provide insight into a majority of the problems and solutions associated with power conditioning equipment in general, and converters in particular.

articleTitle: Newly Developed Meta-Seal SP Underground Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Cables in use in oil refineries, petro-chemical industries or other chemical plants are often left subjected to various sorts of chemical agents, oils and solvents, and we have heretofore experienced many examples of deterioration of such cables. In order to avoid such chemical deterioration, PE-sheathed cables have been mainly in use in those plants.

articleTitle: A New Efficient Method to Evaluate Carrier Channel Performances on Long EHV Power Lines With Transpositions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new mathematical model to evaluating the carrier channel performances on lossy, non-uniform multiconductor transmission lines is presented. Travelling wave the ory is used to define the current and voltage propagation equations on transmission systems which present discontinuity points due to phase transpositions, terminal impedances, shunt-faults. The proposed algorithm makes it possible to compute the voltage attenuation at the generic progressive along the line and in abnormal conditions caused by the presence of a shunt-fault. Practical applications are presented for two long EHV transmission lines with phase transpositions. The results obtained show the effects on voltage attenuation produced by the presence of transpositions and line faults and offer useful indications for the optimal choice of coupling arrangements.

articleTitle: Simulating Central Battery Storage Using A Levelized Incremental Cost Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a methodology for including central battery storage in hourly production simulation computer programs. As such, these simulation tools calculate detailed production statistics by modeling the hour by hour operation of a power system over the planning horizon. An example of such a production analysis code is GLIMPS, described in reference 1-2. By integrating the hourly operation of central storage into the unit commitment and economic dispatch routines, production analysis codes can be used to assess the production credits associated with the storage technologies. These credits can then be used to value central storage by determining the present worth production costs with and without storage over the planning horizon.

articleTitle: Effects of Special Purpose Hardware in Scientific Computation with Emphasis on Power System Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Several uses for special purpose numerical hardware for scientific applications have recently been proposed [1, 3, 6]. However, few of those innovations have yet been implemented. We discuss some of the characteristics essential for an application to effectively use a special purpose processor. We examine some power system applications and argue that their present form is not suitable for systems that include special purpose processors.

articleTitle: Optimum Power Generation and Purchase Balance Under Demand Variations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm to dispatch the electric load of a plant among its power feeder (tie-line) and in-plant generators such that the best economical mix of purchased and generated power is achieved. The developed algorithm is applicable to a wide class of mix generation-plants, among which is the typical paper mill considered in this study.

articleTitle: Encapsulated Current-Limiting Fuses: Grounded-Front Design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a remedy for grounded-front apparatus which suffers from a lack of desirable current-limiting fuse protection. The encapsulated current-limiting fuse offers solutions to the problems of mounting and available ratings. Design and benefits of the encapsulated fuse are discussed and compared to conventional reusable-housing designs.

articleTitle: The Development of a Distribution Transformer Not Subject to Destructive Failure
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Various materials and processes required for the construction of a nondestructive 15-kV class 50-kVA distribution transformer are being developed. High-temperature paint, low-temperature-melting glass, fiberglass cloth, and porcelain tubes have been used in modeling coils and transformers to prove the feasibility of an inorganically insulated distribution transformer. Techniques and equipment for applying the insulations and winding the coils are being developed.

articleTitle: Computational Techniques for an Electrical Distribution and Information Control System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the network analysis functions that are associated with the Electrical Distribution and Information Control System (EDICS for the real-time monitoring and control of the North York Hydro electrical distribution system. The methods presented can be adapted to any distribution network topology and automated control philosophy. Dynamic color displays are provided to effectively show the electrical state of the network, while a unique analysis method estimates network flows in the presence of circuit loops and feeder parallels. A simulation study subsystem provides a means for the dispatcher to verify the consequences of switching orders before they are issued and to investigate potential overload conditions.

articleTitle: Mixing Process of Arced Gas With Cold Gas in the Cylinder of Gas Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Mixing process of high temperature and low temperature gases in the cylinder during arc back was observed for a model GCB with and without puffer action by shadow method. The volume and the temperature of the mixing region were estimated based on the results of the observation . The rate of volume increase of the mixed gas is expressed as a function of the arc power. The temperature of the mixed gas was found to decrease within ten milli-seconds after the arc initiation to around 300 K and 500 K in the cases with and without puffer action, respectively.

articleTitle: Selection of Distribution Transformer Efficiency Characteristics Based on Total Levelized Annual Costs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A method for selecting the optimum efficiency characteristics for distribution transformers is presented.

articleTitle: Advance Turbine-Generator Controls
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Advanced turbine-generator controls contribute to the utility industry's goal of producing reliable electric power at low cost. This paper describes how the microprocessor-based controllers and monitors aid turbine-generator .Operational flexibility, load cycling, two shift position .Network stability, fast recovery from load rejection .Operator guidance or relief from critical duties Specifically, microprocessor-based controllers calculate critical thermal quantities in the turbine, make and implement decisions, and control turbine startup, loading, and unloading through the positioning of main steam valves.

articleTitle: Fault in Ducte Voltages on Metallic Fencing Located in the Vicinity of a High Voltage Substation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Elements of public safety must be considered when metallic fencing is installed in the fault induced field of a substation. A formula is developed to estimate induced voltage on metallic fencing located adjacent to high voltage substations. A method is presented to estimate grid potential distribution. Verification is made using a fence model alongside a test grid. And, an example is given of a hazardous voltage which could be induced on metallic fencing during a line to ground fault.

articleTitle: The Economic Life of Primary URD Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The economic life of polyethylene insulated primary URD cable is defined as the number of years of service such that continued operation of the cable results in greater cost than its replacnt. Formulation of the economic life shows that it is a function of the failure rate of the cable, discount rate, service restoration cost, replacement cost and the value of unserved energy. under simplifying assumptions, the economic life of a given installation is calculated readily.

articleTitle: Bibliography on Corporate - Financial Models 1964-1980
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a bibliography of selected books, papers and articles on the subject of corporate-financial models.

articleTitle: Models for MIMD Machines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes two simple models for estimating the processing times of algorithms run on MIMD (Multiple Instruction Multiple Data) machines. The first model is developed from very elementary queueing concepts. The second uses the critical path through a PERT-diagram-arrangement of the algorithm's tasks. The models require far less effort than either benchmarking or detailed simulations. We envision them being used in all but the very final stages of the search for, and design of, good combinations of algorithms and MIMD machines.

articleTitle: Corrosion of Concentric Neutrals of Butied URD Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The chemistry of copper concentric neutrals in soil is discussed and related to the corrosion problem. Electrochemical factors such as differential aeration, the presence of an intermetallic in a coating, stray A.C. and D.C. are important in producing corrosion Electrical measurements and their interpretation have an important role in studying the problem.

articleTitle: Behaviour of Impregnated Composite Insulation Under High Voltage at Very Low Frequency
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Low frequency tests using a ramped voltage waveform were conducted on sandwich type composite impregnated insulation consisting of paper and/ or polypropylene. Mineral and silicone oil were used as impregnants. Volt-current plots were used to analyze insulation behaviour. It is shown that the plots are useful in assessing the quality of the insulation. Losses are shown to occur due to inelastic deformation of the insulation.

articleTitle: A Consideration on Dielectric withstand test Method for Dead Tank Type High Voltage Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper describes the necessity to add several items on the existing standard dielectric withstand test for high voltage circuit breakers. These are supplementary chopped wave tests to check performance of ceramic grading capacitors, power frequency test to check the breakers' dielectric withstand capability with existance of metallic particles, and capacitor current switching tests after multiple interruptions of full short circuit current.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Linear Programming Planning Methods for Pumped Storage Hydro
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A linear programming model for electric generation planning has been extended to provide the options required for pumped storage hydro planning. Pumped storage hydro is defined by installed capacity and capacity factor. The corresponding four options desirable planning purposes are the capability to 1) specify capacity factor and solve for optimal installed capacity or 2) solve for both optimal installed capacity and capacity factor. The model calculates the total electric planning strategy that minimizes present worth cost, or any other objective specified by the planner subject to the input option and data base. The planner can also perform the primary and secondary objective analysis via a sequential objective feature.

articleTitle: Dispatcher Training Course: Program, Facilities, and Support Requirements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A Dispatcher Training Course was developed with the main objective being to educate power system dispatchers in the fundamental principles and practices of interconnected system operation and performance.

articleTitle: Reset Characteristics of Automatic Resetting Type Fault Indicators on Three-Phase URD Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The need for reliable fault indication in industrial parks has never been greater than it is today. For the most part, these areas are serviced by three-phase multi-legged core padmount transformers. If single-phasing occurs, a voltage induced in the open leg could cause automatic resetting type fault indicators to incorrectly reset as a result. This paper deals with such a situation and its solution. Studies and tests by Long Island Lighting and RTE determined the magnitude of the incident, its affect on associated equipment, and what new product application information resulted.

articleTitle: A Multi-Microcomputer Based Distributed Front End Communications Subsystem for a Power Control Center
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: As a Power Control Center matures the loading on its main CPU may eventually reach a critical level. A method used at one control center to solve this problem is to add on a front end communications processor to the existing system. A design using standard, off-the-shelf microcomputers is described. The front end system consists of a single sixteen bit microcomputer and multiple eight bit microcomputers used as slave processors. The front end processor is interfaced to the PCC main CPU via a 38.4k baud serial data link. The functions which were offloaded from the main CPU are described along with the development process used to integrate the overall system operation. The results of tests on the new configuration are evaluated to show the actual performance levels.

articleTitle: New Interactive Short-Circuit Calculation Algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new method is presented for the calculation of short-circuit currents and voltages using an iterative technique to form the bus impedance matrix. This approach provides a very efficient interactive algorithm and a high degree of calculating accuracy since it takes account of all shunt elements and off-nominal transformer ratios.

articleTitle: High - Availability Power for MX
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: With modern computer-based analyses it was sible to optimize an extensive power transmission and distribution network for supplying power to MX missile shelter sites. This network would serve some 4600 of these sites, located in suitable contiguous areas, with the shelter sites spaced one mile apart. With a dedicated transmission network and underground distribution cables we were able to predict an average commerical power availability of 0.99993 at the shelters. However, standby diesel generator sets are required at distribution centers because power is required after an electromagnetic pulse from a high-altitude weapon burst. With this strengthened distribution network, we were able to predict a suitable power availability of 0.999 at each missile site with incoming power supplied to each of our distribution centers at a 0.99 availability or better by local public utilities.

articleTitle: Using Capillary Gas Chromatography to Determine Poluchlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs) in Electrical Insulating Liquids
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Under the provisions of the U. S. Toxic Substances Control Act, [1] the U. S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has implemented rules for the handling and disposal of polychlorinated biphenyl-(PCB) contaminated insulating fluids.[2,3,4] To properly handle and dispose of oils, the EPA classifies electrical insulating fluids as non-PCB (0 to 50 ppm), PCB-contaminated (50 to 500 ppm), or PCB (greater than 500 ppm). An improved analysis method is presented for determining both qualitative and quantitative PCBs in insulating fluids. This method uses an acid wash, Florisil isolation of the PCBs from the oil, and capillary gas chromatography analysis.

articleTitle: Package Substation System Type Enk with SF6 Insulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The technical advantages of SF6 gas insulated switchgear are in general well known; however, GIS is mostly used in modular pipe-type designs above 121 kV systems.

articleTitle: Large Adjustable Speed Drives
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Today, high energy costs and the availability of large (Example: 3000A, 4000V) solid- state devices are forcing industry to look at new and different adjustable speed drives. This paper introduces three different types of adjustable able speed drives for use on large fans and mixed flow pumps. The three systems are: (1) the current source inverter; (2) the wound rotor slip recovery system; and (3) the synchro-converter or brushless D.C. system.

articleTitle: Electrical - Mechanical Design of the Bonneville Second Powerhouse
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Development of upstream storage in the existing Columbia River basin made it economically attractive to add a second powerhouse to the existing Bonneville Project. The design problem concerned integrating the new powerhouse into a 40 year old project while meeting environmental constraints in river flow and providing for anadromous fish passage. Scope of treatment involves a general discussion of project ectrical and mechanical features with a review of equipment selected and reasons for selection in Certain cases. The resulting discussion provides information on the design of a large low head hydroelectric powerhouse which began commerical operation in 1981

articleTitle: Characteristics of High-Voltage Current-Limiting Fuses for Distributing Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper reviews the major parameters to be considered when selecting fuses for the protection of transformers, capacitor banks and laterals. Overload, secondary-fault and internal-fault protection as well as fuse immunity to current surges (magnetizing and lightning currents, capacitor and cable charging, and motor start-up) are used to establish the required current ratings and time-current characteristics of fuses.

articleTitle: Houston Lighting & Power's Preliminary Economic Analysis of Load Management
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A preliminary study of alternatives for Houston Lighting & Power Company's load management program is discussed. Combinations of 10 different load management methods were analyzed for short term (1985) and long term (1995) benefits.

articleTitle: New-Type Cable Accessories for Power Distribution
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes new types of cable accessories for improving the reliability of power distribution cable systems. The practical development of a 25kV-class cable termination, and a waterproof sleeve for cable joints based on heat-shrinkable components made of irradiated polyolefine is discussed. Furthermore, the theoretical and practical data are given.

articleTitle: Response of Pressurized Water Reactors to Network Power Generation Demands
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: There is a widely held notion in the electric power generation community that nuclear power plants are, in some way, not well suited for a dynamic role in meeting the varying generation needs of the distribution network. The source of this misconception is not clear. Perhaps it stems from the historic role nuclear power has played in the United States, or from a perceived deficiency in nuclear technology or lack of margins to core safety limits. The purpose of this paper is to dispel such notions by presenting on-line plant data to demonstrate the load following flexibility of a Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR). As background, the factors that affect transient flexibility and the system design features engineered into the PWR to insure continued availability of these capabilities are also discussed.

articleTitle: Communication Needs of the Nuclear Power Plant Operator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Nuclear power plant operators and trainers were interviewed to examine human factors considerations associated with control room operation. One part of this review dealt with communications. Over eighty percent of the interview sample reported problems and frustrations with existing communication systems. The nature of the problems uncovered and future research needs are the subjects of this paper.

articleTitle: 6.9-kV, 63-kA Metal-Clad Switchgear with Vacuum Circuit Breakers for Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The technological advancement for larger capacities of vacuum circuit breakers in recent years has truly been prominent.

articleTitle: Standardized SCADA-AGC System Effect on System Cost, Delivery and Quality
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a new Northern States Power Company SCADA-AGC system and the effects of being forced, by time and economic constraints to purchase highly standardized vendor hardware and software.

articleTitle: Linking Distribution Facilities and Customer Information System Data Bases
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: PGandE has been working for several years on the design and implementation of a Distribution Data Base System (Codename: MIDAS). MIDAS will maintain all gas and electric distribution facilities in geographically related data base form. From this single source it will be possible to perform such functions as drawing maps, analyzing electric circuits and gas networks, and preparing tax reports.

articleTitle: Variable Frequency Starting Equipment for Pumped Storage Projects
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the variable frequency starting equipment for the Bath County Pumped Storage Project now being built by Virginia Electric and Power Company. The principle of operation and the construction are discussed, as well as special considerations with grounding the generator/motor during operation of the starting equipment.

articleTitle: The Bulb-Type Generators of Rock Island Power Station and Their Novel Cooling System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Presentation of a new cooling system for bulb type generators, based upon three principles:-radial stator cooling of quite novel type, using about 100, 000 narrow ducts distributed in the magnetic core and formed by special way of cutting out and stacking the magnetic punchings,-complete independence of stator and rotor gas circuits in spite of radial stator cooling, the hot air flowing from the field coils back to the rotor spider,-transverse cooling of rotor winding. This new cooling system has been successfully applied to the eight 54 MVA generators of Rock Island and allows 100 MW bulb units to be contemplated.

articleTitle: Economics of Heat Loss for Power Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Energy losses occur in power cables which cause a rise in the conductor temperature. A trend toward higher allowable conductor temperatures has increased' the energy losses during operation. At the same time, the costs of the energy has increased dramatically.

articleTitle: Metallographic Study of Dual Type Current Limiting Fuse Element
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A newly developed dual-element current-limiting fuse with full protection capability has fuse element consisting of two sorts of metals, i. e. gold-silicon eutectic alloy wire and silver wire being connected in series. The results of the metallographic study is reported on the process of deterioration of fuse element caused by repetition of over-current using high temperature microscope, an electron probe microanalyzer and a regular optical microscope. It is clarified (1) that fusing of the dual-type current-limiting fuse element does not occur at the silver wire section but always at the gold-silicon eutectic alloy wire, and (2) that fine gold-silicon eutectic structure is unifomly distributed in gold primary crystal even after the repetition of over-current and the eutectic structure is stable up to the melting point.

articleTitle: Development of 7.2 kV-63 kA Advanced Puffer Gas Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Design parameters of puffer type SF6 gas circuit breakers were discussed based on the thermo-gas dynamic simulation of arc quenching phenomenon including the pressure generation by the arc itself. The results of the simulation revealed that the puffer breaker with high interrupting capacity can be designed with much less cylinder volume and much less driving power compared with the breaker designed by the conventional way of increasing the mechanical power to obtain high interrupting capacity. A compact puffer breaker with the interrupting capacity of 63 kA at 7.2 kV was developed based on the simulation.

articleTitle: Magnetizing Current Harmonics Caused by Pulse Burst Modulated Loads
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Pulse Burst Modulated (PBM) circuits inject dc currents into power networks. Non-linear inductances, especially transformers supplying or connected in parallel with PBM loads will be exposed to dc voltages which will cause the operation of the magnetic core to be on an asymmetrical B/H hysteresis loop. This work presents a theoretical model which enables the prediction of magnetizing current harmonics and dc biasing flux caused by a PBM load connected in a circuit with known parameters.

articleTitle: Economic Evaluation of a Novel Underground Transmission System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper provides a discussion of the major elements that should be considered when making a comparative economic analysis of alternative underground transmission systems. Approaches are presented on the methods of accomting for each of the components.

articleTitle: Effects of Partial Load Rejection on Fossil Fuel Utility Steam Generators
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a discussion of the effects of partial load rejection by utility turbine-generators on fossil fuel fired steam generator systems. Available surveys on reliability of steam generators undergoing large decreases in load are examined. Also, specific examples of load rejection are discussed.

articleTitle: Underground High-Power Transmission: First Results of Testing A 110 KV Low-Pressure Oil-Filled Cable with a Water-Cooled Conductor in Berlin (West), Germany
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Berliner Kraft-u. Licht (BEWAG)- AG have been conducting investigations during the last several years On a 110 kV low-pressure oil-filled high-power cable with a water cooled conductor and a load capacity of 950 MVA at 110 kV. After sucessful transport of the cable drums (weight: 16 metric tons; diameter: 4.9 m) from the manufacturing in Cologne, West Germany, to Berlin (West), and after laying of the cable over a 300 m stretch, the commissioning tests in accordance with IEC and VDE* standards have been concluded, and several loadings with a current of 5000 A have been performed. Now, after completion of various improvements in the test system, preparations are underway for initiation of long-term testing over a period of approx. 18 months.

articleTitle: Cogenerative Fueled by Solid Waste Utilizing a New Tecnology
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Energy recovery from solid waste has been common in Europe for many years. In the last 10 years the number of these facilities built in the United States has been increasing. However most of the solid waste energy recovery facilities have been built in large cities such as Nashville, Tennessee, Saugus, Massachusetts, Akron, Ohio, and Chicago, Illinois, using the well-developed water-wall furnaces similar to those found in large utility plants. The technologies available in sizes applicable to smaller communities have been found wanting in reliability and in the capability for producing high pressure steam to drive turbines. The water-wall rotary combustors being installed in a facility in Sumner County, Tennessee, offer the promise of reliability and capability heretofore not available to smaller communities.

articleTitle: Low Magnitude, Non-Violent, Fault Clearing Devides for Use with Current Limiting Fuses
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The use of higher voltages (e.g. 35kV) in underground distribution systems has introduced new problems in control of fault currents. These problems are especially evident in the higher ampacity load current ranges. This problem may be addressed by the use of a low current vacuum interrupter (under 2000 amps) coordinated with a backup current limiting fuse to give full-range fault protection without the operating violence and space requirements of conventional expulsion fuses and at a lower cost than conventional circuit breakers. This approach can provide a full-range, non-violent fault interrupter up through the full-rated load current of present load density requirements.

articleTitle: Boiling Water Reactor (BWR) Control Rooms: The Future is Now!
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Over the past five years, many published references have been made to nuclear plants and "Control Rooms of the future". All of these references have stated there is a need for the application of human factors technology to the design of the "Control Room of the future". This paper will describe the design evolution and the methodology employed to apply human factors technology in a Control Complex now installed in a nuclear power plant. That "future" is now!

articleTitle: Important Performance Criteria for Distribution Line Carrier System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Published performance of distribution line carrier communications confuse or mislead through their lack of standard performance metrics. This paper presents metrics of communication system performance which can be used to evaluate distribution line carrier systems when used over power distribution lines for automatic distribution functions such as load control, feeder automation, meter reading, and load survey. The emphasis in this paper is on fundamental quantities like throughput and residual error rate which are often used to measure the effectiveness of other data transmission systems and networks. A sample, calculation of system requirements is included.

articleTitle: Development of a Multi-Channel Telemetry System with 256 Data Channels
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new telemetry system with 256 data channels was developed to measure stresses, temperature, etc. on generator rotors during normal operation. This system was developed because it is economically impossible to measure so many points using slip rings or standard commercially available telemetry systems which normally have a finite number of data channels. In the system reported here, the rotating sensors are sampled, digitized and their signals transmitted to stationary recording instrumentation. Preliminary tests confirmed that the system can be used to centrifugal accelerations of 4,800 G. with a data accuracy of better than ±0.5%.

articleTitle: Innovative Fusing Techniques for Protecting Shunt-Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The latest information-including a new series of devices-on fuses availableforprotecting shuntcapacitors is presented. The type of fuse to be used on particular types and sizes of capacitor banks is discussed.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of 500-KV Series Capacitor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: No 500-kV series capacitor systems have been in practice yet in Japan, but trend towards increased capacities of power sources and installation thereof at remote locations will necessitate such systems in the near future. To meet future needs, major pieces of equipment for such systems had been under development for years, and a prototype one-phase module of full-size system was constructed recently for performance test purposes. The test results have shown that development of compact, economical 1000-MVar class 500-kV series capacitor systems meeting 5OkA short- circuit, salt contamination and earthquake requirements specific to Japan is possible.

articleTitle: Electric Power Generation from a Geothermal Souce Utilizing a Low-Temperature Organic Rankine Cycle Turbine
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A demonstration project to generate electricity with a geothermal source and low-temperature organic Rankine cycle turbine in a rural Alaskan location is described. Operating data and a set of conclusions are presented detailing problems and recommendations for others contemplating this approach to electric power generation.

articleTitle: Status of Project P666, Design Guide for Electric Power Service Systems for Generating Stations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is a status report to the IEEE Power Engineering Society on a Design Guide for Electric Power Service Systems for Generating Stations. It identifies why a design guide is needed and how it will serve the power industry. Included is a discussion of its scope. The status and content of each Chapter is also included.

articleTitle: Transformer Overcurrent Protection A Ten Point View
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A rapid analysis can be made of overcurrent protection with current magnitudes at only ten points in the time domain using a digital computer with graphics capability. Benefits of this approach include a convenient visual representation and permanent record of the particular application being studied.

articleTitle: Modern Alarm Line Supervisory Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The technical information available to the underworld is increasing. They have made an effort to study and understand alarm system operations. Sophisticated instrumentation is as far as their nearest electronics store. To survive this threat, the alarm industry has had to improve supervisory techniques on their signaling circuits so compromise is no longer a simple substitution. Some of the state-of-the-art methods are described.

articleTitle: Electrical Control Features of the Bonneville Hydroelectric Project
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: With the addition of the second hydroelectric powerhouse at the Bonneville project a method of control of the second powerhouse needed to be designed. The development of this control will be explained by general discussion. A review of the method of integrating the second powerhouse control with the first powerhouse control will present a unique approach taken to the problem. The material presented should provide useful information to anyone confronted with a similar problem.

articleTitle: Test and Service Experience of BNC Impregnated Power Capacitors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Experience from various kinds of tests as well as from service of BNC impregnated power capacitors produced during a 4 year period is reviewed.

articleTitle: Insulated Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Special attention must always be given to the reliability of a distribution system, since its design must be developed regarding the loads to be carried, not only within its operacional flexibility, but also of its components, all associated to the installation, operation and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Obsolescence Evaluation of Process Control Computer Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The determination of when a process control computer system is obsolete and requires replacement is a problem that must be approached in a logical and objective manner. An approach has been developed which uses specific trigger points to determine when a detailed investigation of obsolescence is needed and which defines specific criteria against which the performance and continued suitability of the system can be judged. The methodology described can be applied to any type of process control computer system to give a systematic approach to determining and justifying the need to replace an existing system.

articleTitle: Qualification Testing of Insulated Aerial Devices Rated 69 kV and Below
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Laboratory and field measurements were made at the American Electric Power System facilities to compare the three methods commonly used in the industry for testing insulation of an aerial lift device rated for live-line maintenance work at 69 kV and below. Charging current was measured into the bucket of an insulated 69 kV aerial lift truck, from the truck body to ground, and from permanently installed electrodes in the insulating boom section. The results from one set of field measurements on a 69 kV transmission line compare the three methods, for which current values were 400 µA, 168 µA and 8 µA, respectively. Of the three methods used, the permanently installed electrodes is the only method that adequately approaches the true leakage current through the boom insulation. Tests also demonstrated that the addition of a shield over the electrode (collector band) increased the measurement resolution by reducing the current reading by about 50%.

articleTitle: Zonal Security Technique for Use in Strategic and Tactical Response Planning
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a statistical technique for the determination of the penetration probability of each physical point in the protected facility as a function of time. Knowledge of the actual route or destination of the intruding force is not required. The technique is based on a "state vector" description of the facility in conjunction with a transition matrix. The time evolution is determined by utilization of the "Markov" assumption for the system. While the basic solution utilizes a time independent transition matrix a means of extending the method to a time dependent transition matrix case is described. An example is provided to show how the technique may be utilized in determining a "zonal" security map of the system for use in tactical response planning. Use of the results for strategic planning and for "weak point" determination in the system design is also presented.

articleTitle: Interactive Short Circuit System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: During the past few years, power system engineers have used interactive computing as an aid in solving power system planning problems. Most of the development work has been concentrated in the load flow area. Interactive load flow systems have been implemented on dedicated mini-computers as well as on large general purpose corporate computers.

articleTitle: Lifting of Transmission Towers Under Liver Line Conditions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: To maintain adequate conductor ground clearance under emergency operating conditions, tower raising was required on existing double-circuit 230 kV transmission lines. A special tower lifting system was developed for raising towers while adding tower extensions all without de-energizing the lines. Since the method and equipment was unique, a major performance/acceptance test program was conducted which also served to confirm design assumptions. The system was demonstrated on a three-tower test line.

articleTitle: Work in Progress Tiee Project P821 Guide for Content of Technical Manuals
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the up-to-date draft of a document being prepared by a working group of the Station Design Subcaiittee of the Power Generation Committee, on the preparation of Technical Manuals.

articleTitle: Testing Facilities for Developing UHV Equipments
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The testing facilities of UHV (Ultra High Voltage) laboratory are described in this paper. The voltage rating of testing facilities and dimensions of the laboratory for developing UHV substation equipments, especially transformers and gas insulated equipments, are discussed on the basis of research and development experiencies of UHV equipment manufacture.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of 15kV to 35kV Porcelain Terminations Using New Connection Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: New techniques for conductor connection in underground cable terminations were investigated in a design of a new distribution class porcelain cable termination. Connections to the conductor were accomplished using set screws, building upon previous designs with additions to assure a conservative design approach. The connector design was tested according to applicable standards for load cycling of connections, and the result appears capable of conservative performance in the operating environment.

articleTitle: Human Factors in Control Room Design a Matter of Decision and Implementation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: TMI-2 focused attention on Human Engineering deficiencies in all nuclear plant control rooms while overlooking the evolution of their design and the principles of good system design. Reasons for the less than desirable features of the control rooms are explained. Standardization and modularization of board structure and board-mounted components are proposed to help achieve improvement in the designs. Mockups and more extensive use of C.R.T.' s are urged. A method of "Usage" or task analysis is presented and the importance of operator participation is emphasized.

articleTitle: Evaporative Cooling of Power Cables - Prediction of Steady State Operation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The concept is discussed of cooling a power cable by the natural convective flow of a coolant in the conductor duct. The following quantities are determined at a given distance from the conductor duct entrance; gas/liquid content (void fraction), heat- transfer coefficient, temperature, flow quality and pressure. For a given reservoir head and cable loading (i.e. heat input) the permissible length of cooled cable is determined such that certain constraints are obeyed.

articleTitle: Human Engineering Guidelines for Desing and Operations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Recognizing the need for human engineering in the design of nuclear power plants, the Electric Power Research Institute established a project to develop human engineering criteria and principles in a guidebook format for application to nuclear power plants design. Using the technology evolving from the Armed Forces human engineering effort, the Essex Corporation devised a guidebook composed primarily of quantitative data and functional relationships supporting the nuclear power plant design process which is fully indexed for easy use and looseleaf in format for convenient updating. The development approach employing potential guidebook users to verify the completeness, relevance, and usefulness of material content and format is presented along with an organizational outline for the guidebook.

articleTitle: The Construction of a Forced-Cooled Distribution Duct Bank
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The article describes a method used for the construction of a prototype forced-cooled distribution duct bank in the Hydro-Quebec network. The method is especially suited to the cooling of multi-cable duct banks leading out of sub-stations which supply congested urban areas. Forced cooling is achieved by the circulation of water through two ducts of the bank and through an air-cooled heat exchanger at the sub-station. The procedure entails the determination of the cooling requirements and the choice of equipment for the cooling system and for the appropriate control and alarm systems. Results show that the construction of such a system is feasible with a possible economic saving.

articleTitle: Multi-Power Port Gas Turbine Configurations for Solar Cogeneration Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Solar energy, unlike fossil fuel energy, is a constrained source of power. It is constrained by its diurnal and seasonal variations and by weather upsets. Solar energy, unlike fossil fuel energy, which is highly concentrated and highly commandable, cannot be directly commanded. The only means to control the solar power input to a gas turbine is the flow rate of the fluid which acquires the converted solar heat and conveys it, passing through the turbine stages on its way to the exhaust. A conventional gas turbine set has one power input port, the combustion heat-compressed gas at the gas turbine inlet, and one controlled power power output port, the mechanical variable shaft torque of the power turbine. For cogeneration applications, two power controlled ports are necessary: the mechanical shaft torque--usually used to drive a generator--and the exhaust fluid--usually compressed clean air for industrial or topping cycle uses.

articleTitle: Guide to Power Station Noise Control - A Working Group Report
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Due to increased megawatt unit sizes in the traditionally noisy power stations, noise emission levels have increased considerably. Regulations and public concern have increased the importance of reducing the harmful effects of this noise. IEEE recognized the need for industry guidance in this difficult area and formed a working group to consolidate expertise and report on the subject of power station audible noise control. Background is provided on the process of developing "the guide" report. The guide content is reviewed with emphasis on the systematic steps in consideration for a typical noise control program and how the guide assists in this regard.

articleTitle: "How to Achieve High Reliability in Medium Voltage Terminations"
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses a specific test sequence based on the well known worldwide standards for medium voltage terminations. This sequence tests the three basic aspects of the termination. That is, performance as newly manufactured, performance after aging, and performance under wet environments ( either indoor or outdoors.). Brazilian electrical mnufacturers are now studying such test sequences and will soon be standardizing.

articleTitle: A Numerical Analysis of Load-Flow Calculation Methods [Discussion and Closure]
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The above-named article was published in IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems, Vol. PAS-100, No. 7, July 1981, pp. 3642-3647. The Discussion and Closure were not available at the time of publication. They are presented here.

articleTitle: Rating Limits for Generator/Motors for High Head Pumped Storage Projects
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Economics of scale can assume unusual importance in the case of pumped storage schemes involving underground reservoirs. The paper proposes an approach to define the presently attainable maximum ratings for generator/motors in the 514-1200 RPM speed range. Prelimimary results are presented as well as directions for confirming and/or extending these limits.

articleTitle: Analysis of Anchor Corrosion on Two Parallel Coastal Transmission Power Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Corrosion problems of two 230 kV overhead transmission lines located in extensive coastal zones are analyzed. The lines are parallel on the same rights-of-way, but use different grounding techniques. Step-by-step testing procedures are introduced. The data is presented in a table with corresponding charts and figures. Economic analysis is used to study possible solutions. Three examples are given which address the cost of anchor protection vs. the existing situation continuing. Recommendations are made for the lines studied, and for future construction in low resistivity soils.

articleTitle: Vital Area Penetration Significance
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The use of Fault Tree Analysis has recently been recognized by security design engineers as a valuable tool in determining the protection levels which should be applied to various areas in the protected facility. This paper describes how these techniques may be extended to provide the engineer with an assessment of the significance of each of the previously defined vital areas. The technique utilizes point penetration probabilities for each of the areas to provide an index which measures the impact of penetrating the area in question upon the overall security of the facility. The effect of varying the penetration resistance of each area is then investigated. An example is provided to show how the technique is utilized by the design engineer to determine design requirements for each of the areas. While this technique has been specifically applied in this paper to the security field, it is also applicable to assessing the impact of variations in individual component reliabilities in a standard Fault Tree Analysis.

articleTitle: "In Service Electrical Testing of Live Line Tools" - A Status Report of the Guide
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Historically live line tools have had a remarkable safety record in the hands of the user.

articleTitle: System Design Considerations for Implementing Performance and Service Tests on Class 1E Batteries in Accordance with IEEE 450-1980
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Extensive electrical system design considerations are required to implement performance and service tests on Class 1E batteries in accordance with IEEE 450-1980 "Recommended Practice For Maintenance, Testing and Replacement of Large Lead Storage Batteries for Generating Stations and Substations."

articleTitle: Evolving Fault Performance of Vacuum Switchgear on an 11kV Distribution System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The evolving fault, a fault condition in which a fault rapidly changes in physical nature immediately after its initiation, has long been known to exist but has rarely been examined on a power distribution system. This paper describes a series of tests which were performed on the Egyptian Electricity Authority's 11kV distribution system in Cairo, and which included simulations of the evolving fault. The paper also describes the capability of the vacuum interrupter to successfully interrupt the evolving fault, and some very unusual, unanticipated, fault current levels.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of a Prestresseed Concrete Pole Section
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper attacks the analysis of prestressed concrete structures. The attack is made assuming that the steel prestress members behave linearly and that the concrete is a nonlinear material obeying a second order stress-strain relationship. The entire analysis depends only on one empirical assumption and is developed from fundamental concepts of statics. The theoretical ground work is presented; and, then, a familiar example is solved. Additional theoretical development is presented as the solution of the example problem develops. This particular method of analysis presents an alternative to the empirically based ACI method.

articleTitle: Dual Feeder 34.5 kV System for S-O Paulo-Brazil
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An accelerated demographic increment of the city of Sao Paulo is forcing decentralisation of the commercial activity and creating new residencial areas. This results in a series of problems for the utilities.

articleTitle: Processing Encapsulated Electrical Products Using Pressure-Gelation Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The study of epoxy-resin processing techniques revealed a preference for the pressure-gelation process. This paper compares this method to alternatives, and presents its advantages and principal steps in the process.

articleTitle: Status Report on Electric Heat Tracing Standards Writing Activities
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper was prepared for presentation at the 1981 Joint Power Generation Conference for the purpose of educating and updating the industry as to what IEEE Standards have been and are. being prepared for use in designing and installing electric heat tracing systems in generating stations. The paper gives a brief description and explanation of electric heat tracing systems and how they are used, and then moves on to discussions of-IEEE Std. 622-1979, IEEE P622A, and proposed IEEE P622B. The discussions of the above listed standards cover such areas as the reasons for producing the standards, history of their development, controversial aspects of the standards and industry acceptance of the standards. Also discussed in this paper are plans of the Working Group for the development of future IEEE Standards.

articleTitle: Automated Graphics Applications - Drafting
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The approaches to the use of automated graphics (A/G) are probably as varied as the personalities of the people and the organizations involved. Interested concerns beginning to investigate the use of automated graphics may wish to consider this paper as offering a different approach. Pennsylvania Power & Light Co. (PP&L) is not following the traditional utility mapping A/G application. This paper presents considerations similar to interests supporting a variety of engineering design applications.

articleTitle: A Multi-Level Distributed Microprocessor System for a Nuclear Power Plant Fire Protection System Controls, Monitoring, and Communication
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: All nuclear power plants must have fire monitoring and fire suppression systems. The design, construction and operation of these systems involve considerable skill and considerable cost. The instrumentation and control requirements are extensive and sophisticated. Adequate reference works for these requirements and how to achieve them are not available. This paper is an attempt to describe these instrumentation and control requirements and also to present a specific design concept. This incorporates the result of the writer's experience in working with the design review and commissioning the instrumentation and controls of the entire fire detection and suppression system in an operational nuclear power plant and his subsequent study on the subject.

articleTitle: Evaporative Cooling of Power Cables - Prediction of Thermal Performance with Load Changes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The transient thermal performance of evaporatively cooled cable systems utilising the change of phase of Freon 12 is investigated. Methods for computing the temperature-time movements with changes in load or loss of coolant flow are reported. For the internal duct system the change in conductor temperature is seen to be rapid with a step change of load as it is with a loss of coolant. A study, of various cable loading indicates that at an intermediate cable loss the coolant flow rate is a maximum and that flow is maintained over a wide range of loads.

articleTitle: Accurate Modelling of Frequency-Dependent Transmission Lines in Electromagnetic Transient Simulations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The parameters of transmission lines with ground return are highly dependent on the frequency. Accurate modelling of this frequency dependence over the entire frequency range of the signals is of essential importance for the correct simulation of electromagnetic transient conditions. Closed mathematical solutions of the frequency-dependent line equations in the time domain are very difficult. Numerical approximation techniques are thus required for practical solutions. The oscillatory nature of the problem, however, makes ordinary numerical techniques very susceptible to instability and to accuracy errors. The, methods presented in this paper are aimed to overcome these numerical difficulties.

articleTitle: Selective Modal Analysis with Applications to Electric Power Systems, PART I: Heuristic Introduction
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Selective Modal Analysis (or SMA) is a physically motivated framework for understanding, simplifying and analyzing complicated linear time-invariant models of dynamic systems, see [1,2]. SMA can accurately and efficiently focus on selected portions of the structure and behavior of the system. the part of the model that is relevant to the dynamics of interest is singled out in a direct manner, and. the remainder of the model is collapsed in a way that leaves the selected structure and behavior Intact. The paper heuristically presents basic concepts and results of SMA and lays the foundations for their application to a number of problems in analysis of power system dynamics. The approach is illustrated with several examples, including a 60-machine model of a dynamic instability occurrence in an actual power system. A companion paper [3] elaborates on specific applications of SMA to power systems, particularly to the Dynamic Stability problem.

articleTitle: Optimal Spot Pricing: Practice and Theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new concept of electricity pricing referred to as "spot pricing" is presented. Spot pricing is shown to encompass and achieve more fully the objectives of load management techniques and other rate structures proposed so far. The contribution of this paper is the derivation of optimal spot prices and a discussion of and proposals on a number of implementation issues which arise when the theory of spot pricing is turned into practice. A set of rates related to optimal spot prices are proposed and their applicability is discussed in view of different customer characteristics, metering, and communication costs. The impact of spot pricing on line losses and reactive energy, the quality of supply and rationing is elaborated. Issues related to customer response, utility revenues, investments and generation deregulation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Harmonic Power Flow Studies Part I - Formulation and Solution
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The conventional Newton-Raphson power flow study has been reformulated to permit the inclusion of non-linear loads. These loads give rise to harmonic signals which propagate throughout the power system. The reformulation is based on the reduction-to zero of the mismatch active power and reactive voltamperes, the imbalahce current at harmonic frequencies, and the mismatch apparent voltamperbs. Conclusions on the existance of positive, negative, and zero sequence signals is made for harmonic frequencies. The harmonic power flow study formulation is illustrated for a three phase full wave bridge rectifier.

articleTitle: Load Representation in Power System Stability Studies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Proper representation of load is important in power system stability studies, but it is a difficult task. Load modeling is qualitatively different from generator modeling in many aspects. Composition of load needs to be reliably estimated, models of different components must be combined to obtain a reasonably manageable overall system model, and field measurements are not at all easy.

articleTitle: Selective Modal Analysis With Applications to Electric Power Systems, Part II: The Dynamic Stability Problem
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Selective Modal Analysis (or SMA) is a physically motivated framework for understanding, simplifying and analyzing complicated linear time-invariant (or LTI) models of dynamic systems [1,2,3]. SMA allows one to focus on any prespecified dynamic pattern of intrest in the model. In particular, One can efficiently and accurately compute the eigene values and eigenvectors of the natural modes of interest and their sensitivities, and also determine physically meaningful reduced order models containing these natural modes. SMA is particularly suitable for dealing with composite models, i.e. models consisting of several dynamic subsystems interrelated by static constraints. An introduction to the basic concepts of SMA pertinent to the applications being considered here is presented in the companion paper [3]. This paper concerns the application of SMA to the Dynamic Stability problem in electric power systems; it is shown how SMA is well suited to meet the demanding requirements of Dynamic Stability analysis. This is illustrated in [3] with examples, including a 60-machine model of a dynamic instability occurrence in an actual power system.

articleTitle: Load-Flow Solutions for Ill-Conditioned Power Systems by a Newton-Like Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In this paper mathematician K.M. Brown's method is used to solve load-flow problems. The method is Particularly effective for solving of ill-conditioned non- linear algebraic equations. It is a variation of Newton's method incorporating Gaussian elimination in such a way that the most recent infonnation is always used at each step of the algorithm; similar to what is done in the Gauss-Seidel process. The iteration converges locally and the convergence is quadratic in nature. A general discussion of ill-conditioning of a system of algebraic equations is given, and it is also show by the fixed-point formulation that the proposed method falls in the general category of sucessive approximation methods. Digital computer solutions by the proposed method are given for cases for which the standard load-flow methods failed to converge, namely 11-, 13- and 43-bus ill-conditioned test systems. A comparison of this method with the standard load-flow methods is also presented for the well-conditioned AEP 30-, and 57-bus systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to the Torsional Interaction and Electrical Damping of the Synchronous Machine Part I: Theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The torsional interaction phenomenon between the electrical and mechanical system is explained with the aid of the newly introduced complex torque coefficients kͤ(jλ) and kͫ(jλ).
